latin: Quod dixit Anchelos chaldeus becadmin, id est cum aeternis uel per
latin_note: Farmer's transcription as extracted for this inventory breaks off after 'per', apparently at the copy-text's line end. Wirszubski's own transcription of the same conclusio gives the sentence complete: 'Quod dixit anchelos chaldeus becadmin, id est cum aeternis uel peraeterna, triginta duas uias sapientiae intellexit' (wirszubski1989:2370); the apparatus records the 1486/1487 variant 'becadmim' and the 1487 variant 'cum eternis vel paterna' (farmer1998:18090).
translation: What Onkelos the Chaldean said, 'becadmin' -- that is, 'with' or 'through the eternal things' -- he understood [as referring to] the thirty-two paths of wisdom.
translation_note: Translated from the complete sentence as transmitted by Wirszubski's transcription (wirszubski1989:2370), since the locator's own text as extracted stops short of the verb; 'Anchelos' is Onkelos, traditional author of the Aramaic Targum Onkelos, mentioned often by Maimonides and other medieval sources known to Pico (farmer1998:18101); the 'thirty-two paths of wisdom' come from the proto-Kabbalistic Sefer Yetzirah and later texts, on the world's creation through the twenty-two Hebrew letters and the ten sefirot (farmer1998:18101).
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch11, from Latin at farmer1998:18069
doctrine: Farmer identifies 'Anchelos' as Onkelos the Proselyte, traditional author of the Aramaic Targum Onkelos, frequently mentioned by Maimonides and other medieval sources available to Pico, and traces the 'thirty-two paths of wisdom' to the proto-Kabbalistic Sefer Yetzirah (Book of Creation) and later texts holding that God created the world by the combined power of the twenty-two Hebrew letters and the ten sefirot; he cross-references Pico's magical conclusions at 9>19ff. and 11>58 (farmer1998:18101).
context: Farmer cross-references 9>19, which holds that voices and words have efficacy in magical operation because the voice is the first thing through which nature exercises magic (farmer1998:25366) (farmer1998:18101).
historiography: Wirszubski transcribes theses 28.25 and 28.26 together as his 'Conclusiones XXV and XXVI' and gives the complete Latin text of 28.26 (wirszubski1989:2365, 2368).

quotations.text: Idem est bresith, id est in principio creauit, ac si dixisset in sapientia creauit. Quod dixit anchelos chaldeus becadmin, id est cum aeternis uel peraeterna, triginta duas uias sapientiae intellexit.

not_established: Farmer's further cross-reference to 11>58 on the magical conclusions is not established beyond the bare locator (farmer1998:18101).
not established by the sources consulted
